summary: I sent the exact brief. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read NOTES.md and the four UI guideline docs, then hit an auto-compaction (the skill was restored afterwards). After that it said the task was bounded and the design would stay in chat. It started the visual companion with scripts/start-server.sh, gave me a localhost URL with a key, and wrote filter-placement.html showing three candidate layouts (A, B, C). I picked C. The agent wrote a "layout chosen" waiting screen and asked its two non-visual follow-up questions in the terminal. It then gave the full design in chat and asked for approval. After I said yes, it started editing public/activity.{html,css,js}. It wrote no spec file, no plan file, and never called writing-plans.
reasoning: All 8 criteria pass, based on the session log, the files on disk and the screen. The companion opened only once the layout question arose, after the compaction. It showed the three layouts in HTML, and the task stayed on the bounded path with no spec and no plan. The agent got approval before writing code and then started implementing.

observations.description: The Claude Code onboarding dialogs ('trust this folder' and 'Bypass Permissions') both start with the cursor on 'No, exit'. Pressing Enter by mistake would exit. This is normal Claude Code behaviour, not a bug in the skill.

At startup Claude Code showed 'Newer Opus model available. Currently pinned: Opus 5', even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose 'No', and the banner then showed Opus 5.5. The pinned-model message seems inconsistent with the --model flag.
The agent called the companion 'token-intensive' and offered to stay in the terminal. That's reasonable, but it may make users hesitate.
The agent pointed out that .hyperpowers/ isn't in .gitignore, so the mockup files show up as untracked in git status. The skill could add a .gitignore entry itself, or offer to.

After I picked a layout, the agent said 'One more thing before I start the design', even though it had already settled the layout. The wording is a little confusing. It then asked two terminal questions, which fit the scope, before giving the full design.

Auto-compaction ran twice in a short session: once right after the guideline reading, and again right after I approved. That second one delayed implementation by about a minute. After the compaction the agent re-read the guideline files, which costs extra tokens.

The agent noticed that the page breaks the project's no-JS rule and that the token sheet it refers to doesn't exist, and asked about both separately. Good catch: these are real problems in the fixture.
